sections.heading: Venerable Emilianos, Bishop of Cyzikos, the Confessor

pairs.en: On the same day, the eighth of the month, we remember our venerable father EMILIANOS, bishop of Cyzikos, the confessor.
*Setting the word of his soul far above all else,* *Emilianos gave no thought to the flesh until the end.* *On the eighth the earth received the bones of Emilianos.*

This saint endured many hardships and exiles and afflictions for the veneration of the holy icons, at the hands of the beast-named Leo (perhaps the Armenian), in the year 813; and having ended his life amid these sufferings, he received from the Lord the unfading crown of confession.

sections.heading: Saint Myron, Bishop of Crete, the Wonderworker

pairs.en: On the same day we remember Saint MYRON, bishop of Crete, the wonderworker.
*Myron the godly, breathing the myrrh of virtue,* *comes before the Lord as a fragrance of sweetness.*

He was born in a city of Crete called Avrachia, which lies near Knossos, adorning his family with piety towards God. When he came of age, he was joined in lawful marriage and worked the land; and out of the yield and income of his crops he gave alms to the poor — and the more he gave, the more the fruit of his fields increased.

This saint's sympathy and tender-heartedness towards the poor were beyond anything human. They say that one day the saint caught ten men on his threshing-floor stealing his grain; they had filled their sacks so full — from the sheer weight of the load, and from their greed to take more — that they could no longer lift the sacks, yet neither would they bring themselves to empty a little out. So the saint caught them, and instead of beating them and punishing them for the theft, the man of blessed memory felt sorry for them; with his own hands he helped each one, and they hoisted the sacks onto their shoulders. And not only that: he ordered them not to reveal the matter to anyone, so that he would not lose the reward of his almsgiving and his forbearance.

For these virtues, then, he was ordained a priest in the Church of God; and when the persecution of the Christians came to an end, he ascended the episcopal throne and became Archbishop of Crete. There he worked many mighty deeds and wonders. He drove away a dragon that was ravaging that country, in which it had its lair. He blocked the flow of a river called the Triton, because when the saint was about to cross it, it had flooded. The river, stopped from flowing by the saint's command, ran no further forward as it used to, but stood held back until the saint returned and crossed over again. And when he had gone home, he sent his staff with certain men, who stirred the river water with the saint's staff and made the river run again in its natural course. Having worked these and many more wonders, and having passed the remainder of his life in a manner pleasing to God and holy, and having kept the feasts of the holy martyrs with splendid celebrations, the blessed Myron departed to the Lord, already an old man of a hundred years.
(Note that his wondrous life, his service, and his venerable head are kept at his venerable monastery called Ladodea, in the province of Grevena.)
We remember our venerable father THEODOSIOS, abbot of Oroboi.
*You were shown a very gift of God, blessed one, by your life —* *your way of living proved a fitting advocate of your name.*

This saint, having lifted the cross of the Lord onto his shoulders from his early youth, made his dwelling among the mountains and the caves and the ravines. And so, having been perfected in peace, he was offered up to God like precious myrrh, and like incense acceptable and most fragrant.
(Note that in the Menaia this saint is written as Theodore.)

sections.heading: Holy Martyrs Eleutherios and Leonides, and the Holy Infants

pairs.en: We remember the holy martyrs ELEUTHERIOS and LEONIDES, and the holy infants, who died by fire. Their gathering is kept at the church of Saint Eirene, across the water at Ioustinianai.
*Two athletes who would not sacrifice to error —* *the erring ones sentence them to flame as their punishment.*

sections.heading: The Ten Venerable Ascetics of Egypt

pairs.en: The holy TEN venerable ascetics of Egypt died in peace.
*Ten offshoots of Egypt die —* *equal in number to those ten plagues of hers.*
The holy TWO martyrs of Tyre died dragged along the ground.
*A team wears down the earth, whose cart-pole is the fear of God,* *faith their yoke-strap, and eagerness their wheels.*
(The cart-pole — ῥυμός in the Greek — is the lengthwise timber set in the middle of a cart, the upright piece that hangs from the yokes and tapers to a point. Some copies wrongly read “rhythm.”)
The holy martyr STYRAKIOS died by the sword.
*Cut down by the sword, Styrakios gave off* *a spiritual fragrance, a very storax of the spirit.*

sections.heading: The Dedication of the Church of the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul — and the Eclipse of the Sun

pairs.en: We keep the dedication of the church of the holy Apostles PETER and PAUL, in the precinct of the holy apostle and evangelist John the Theologian, inside the august church of the most-holy Mother of God in the district of Marchachiou, and of Saint Kassianos.

And we keep the remembrance of the time when the eclipse of the sun took place, from the sixth hour until the ninth, so that even the stars appeared, in the year 6399 from the creation of the world (AD 891), the sun being in its fifteenth cycle, and the moon in the same cycles, in the ninth indiction, in the reign of Leo the Wise and of Alexander his brother, the pious and Christ-loving emperors.
(Note that Alexander is styled emperor only as an honour.)

sections.heading: Holy New Martyr Anastasios the Bulgarian

pairs.en: The holy new martyr ANASTASIOS the Bulgarian, who bore witness in Thessalonica in the year 1794, died having endured tortures.
*Anastasios, giving his body over to the tortures,* *found an ending entirely free of pain.*
(Note that his martyrdom is to be found in the New Martyrologion.)

sections.heading: Holy New Martyr Triantaphyllos of Zagora

pairs.en: The holy new martyr TRIANTAPHYLLOS of Zagora, who bore witness in Constantinople in the year 1680, died.
*Triantaphyllos was seen to be a new rose,* *dyed crimson by the stream of his blood.*
(Note that his martyrdom is to be found in the New Martyrologion.)

The calendar of the Ecumenical Patriarchate commemorates on this day also Saint Gregory of Sinai and of Mount Athos, and Saint Kallinikos of Edessa and Pella — whom Nikodemos does not carry in his Synaxarion of 1868.
Through the prayers of your Saints, Christ our God, have mercy on us.
